record_type_quote: The authors use an advertising context to replicate and extend ﬁndings of Kees and colleagues’ (2010) study of the direct and indirect effects of graphic pictorial cigarette warnings.

targets.authors: Kees, Jeremy, Scot Burton, J. Craig Andrews, and John Kozup
targets.title: Tests of Graphic Visuals and Cigarette Package Warning Combinations: Implications for the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control
targets.evidence_quote: Despite extension to the use of updated, currently required text warnings, ad context, and (controversial) pictorial stimuli that were selected by the FDA, cessation-related outcomes replicate ﬁndings and conclusions of Kees and colleagues (2006, 2010).
targets.outcome_quote: Despite extension to the use of updated, currently required text warnings, ad context, and (controversial) pictorial stimuli that were selected by the FDA, cessation-related outcomes replicate ﬁndings and conclusions of Kees and colleagues (2006, 2010).

targets.authors: Kees, Jeremy, Scot Burton, J. Craig Andrews, and John Kozup
targets.title: Understanding How Graphic Pictorial Warnings Work on Cigarette Packaging
targets.evidence_quote: First, we draw speciﬁcally from the work of Kees and colleagues (2010); we seek to replicate their empirical ﬁndings that more graphic pictorial cigarette warnings positively inﬂuence smoking cessation intentions and that evoked fear is a primary mechanism underlying this relationship.
targets.outcome_quote: In addition, in contrast to the ﬁndings of Kees and colleagues (2010), here the moderate graphic examined in Study 2 led to results that were similar to the high graphic pictorial initially selected for use by the FDA.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Cessation and fear-mediated effects agree, but the authors explicitly contrast the moderate-versus-high comparison with the 2010 finding. The concluding confirmation names particular effects rather than an overall verdict over the entire replication.

reasoning: New samples retest published pictorial-warning effects. Both 2006 and 2010 are explicitly identified as findings replicated, while other cited studies supply context or materials.
